body:
`scripts/verification-sweep.sh:124-126`:

```
gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --limit 300 \
  --json number,title,author,labels,comments > "$WORK/issues.json" 2>/dev/null \
  || fail_soft "could not list issues"
```

`2>/dev/null` discards gh's stderr, so the only record of a radar failure is the
literal string "could not list issues". Rate limit, network blip, auth expiry,
GraphQL timeout on a 300-issue comment fetch and a malformed `--json` field all
produce the identical line.

OBSERVED 2026-08-06: the 18:06Z tick logged `status=failed reason=could not list
issues`, streak 1 after ~20 consecutive OK ticks. Determining it was transient
required re-running the exact call by hand (rc=0, 107 issues, 3.6s). The log
could not distinguish "blip, ignore" from "wedged, act."

Why it matters more than a normal swallowed error: this step is the regression
radar. It is deliberately fail-soft and exit-0 so a broken sweep cannot abort the
tick, and the tick pages the operator only at streak >= 3. Those two together
mean the failure reason is the *only* signal available for two whole ticks, and
it currently carries no information. The `wedge-audit-signal-not-just-heal`
lesson applies directly: a path that stops work needs to say why, not just that.

Fix shape: capture stderr into the fail_soft message, e.g.
`ERR="$(... 2>&1 >"$WORK/issues.json")" || fail_soft "could not list issues: ${ERR##*$'\n'}"`,
keeping the reason on one line so the tick's `summary: status=` grep still parses.

Note the sibling risk while touching this: the query pulls `comments` for up to
300 issues in one GraphQL call, which is the kind of request that starts timing
out as the tracker grows. If that is what failed here, the reason string is also
what would have revealed it.
title: verification-sweep discards gh's stderr, so the regression radar's failure reason is unrecoverable
